solutionSql:
SELECT s.customer_id,
       i.id,
       ROUND(AVG(i.amount) OVER (
         PARTITION BY s.customer_id
         ORDER BY i.issued_at, i.id
         ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
       ), 2) AS moving_avg
FROM invoices i
JOIN shipments s ON s.id = i.shipment_id
ORDER BY s.customer_id, i.issued_at, i.id;

rules.howSolved: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW gives each invoice and up to two earlier ones for the same customer. The first invoice averages only itself, and the second averages two.
ROUND(AVG(...), 2) rounds the average after it is computed.

ambiguities: Rounding is read as PostgreSQL ROUND on numeric, which rounds exact halves away from zero. A half-cent average would round up under that reading. A probe found no half-cent averages in sample, ties or precision.
notes: Sample returns 205 rows, ties 154, precision 154. A correlated formulation that averages the last three rows explicitly gives 0 differences on all three datasets.
